overall: Atlanta has had a warmer-than-model-expected day, with the running maximum of 93.2°F established around 17:00 ET and unchanged through 20:30 ET. The current temperature of 87.8°F is cooling at a brisk -1.8°F/hr, confirming the peak has passed. The day trended steadily upward from the morning through mid-afternoon before plateauing, a classic warm-season diurnal pattern.
forecast_obs_notes: All four models (GFS 92.6, ECMWF 91.9, HRRR 92.6, NBM 92.2) underforecast the observed high by 0.6–1.3°F, with consensus clustering near 92.2–92.6°F versus the actual 93.2°F already in the books. Model agreement was tight but collectively ran a bit cool today, possibly underestimating afternoon mixing or boundary-layer heating.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked at 93.2°F since 17:00 ET and temperatures now falling steadily at nearly 2°F/hr into the evening, it is near-certain the daily high has already been set. There is no credible scenario for a new peak this late in the day absent a highly anomalous warm surge, which the current velocity and dewpoint give no indication of. Confidence is very high that 93.2°F is the final TMAX.
